subject: Copywriting
title: Subject Lines: The Email Headline
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Subject Lines: The Email Headline.

hook.text: Obama's 2012 campaign raised $690 million by email. The top-performing subject line was just one word: 'Hey.'

buildup.text: Email subject lines are headlines for the inbox. 47% of recipients decide to open based solely on the subject.

discovery.text: Personal, casual subjects outperform formal ones. 'Quick question' beats 'Important Business Update' every time.

twist.text: The 'Hey' subject worked once. When everyone copied it, open rates crashed. Every trick has a shelf life.

climax.text: Great subject lines follow headline rules: specificity, curiosity, and a clear promise of value inside.

punchline.text: One word: 'Hey.' $690M raised. Subject lines matter.

quiz.question: What was the top-performing email subject line for Obama's campaign?

details.summary: Email subject lines are the headlines of the inbox — the single element that determines whether a message is opened or ignored. With average open rates around 20%, 80% of email content goes unread because the headline failed. Subject line craft is the most impactful skill in email marketing.
details.whyItMatters: Every email marketer is fundamentally a headline writer. The subject line is where the battle for attention is won or lost, making it the highest-leverage element in email copy.
takeaways: Subject lines determine whether 80% of email content is ever read
The best subject lines combine curiosity with clear value promise
Mobile truncation means the first 30 characters must carry the message

faq.question: How are email subject lines similar to newspaper headlines?
faq.answer: Both compete for split-second attention decisions. Both must communicate value instantly. Both are judged alongside competitors (other emails, other articles). The key difference is that subject lines also compete with personal messages from friends and family.

faq.question: What is the ideal length for an email subject line?
faq.answer: Studies suggest 30-50 characters perform best because they display fully on mobile. But length matters less than content — a compelling 60-character subject outperforms a boring 30-character one. Lead with the most important words in case of truncation.
